summary.headline: Shilpa Medicare posted record Q2 FY27 revenue of INR538 crores (+35% YoY) and EBITDA of INR151 crores at a 28% margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered record quarterly revenue (INR538 crores, +35% YoY) and record EBITDA (INR151 crores, +37% YoY), with H1 revenue crossing INR1,000 crores for the first time. Growth was broad-based across API, formulation and biologics. Gross margin compressed by roughly 700 bps YoY and sequentially, as raw material cost to sales rose from 28.65% to 35.72%, which management attributed to higher API sales and global API raw material inflation. Net debt was steady at INR612 crores despite INR252 crores of H1 capex funded from internal accruals. Management gave no revenue or utilisation guidance on peptides, albumin or Rotigotine beyond timing milestones.

segments.name: Non-captive API
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR255 crores (+24% YoY); H1 INR470 crores (+20% YoY), driven by uptake from expanded capacity and steady specialty CDMO. Management said API delivered its highest-ever quarterly revenue, and it stopped splitting oncology and non-oncology revenue.

segments.name: Formulation
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR210 crores (+50%+ YoY); H1 INR407 crores (+70% YoY). Excluding licensing income, the base business grew 87% in the quarter, led by EU complex finished dosage formulations. India business grew 2.5x in H1, led by Nor-UDCA.

segments.name: Biologics
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR65 crores (+150% YoY); H1 INR117 crores (+92% YoY), driven by licensing and partnership deals and CDMO. Management says biologics is 12% of revenue and only Adalimumab is commercially supplied in the market.

segments.name: CDMO (newly carved out as Shilpa CDMO platform)
segments.commentary: 25-plus NCE CDMO programs; 4 late-stage programs under registration and 2 in Phase III. Management expects at least one commercialisation next year and three the year after. No CDMO revenue split was disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management gave no formal revenue or earnings guidance; it said the business has good traction and momentum should continue.
Expects ROCE to improve as plant capacities fill and business mix shifts to high-margin peptides, oncology APIs and CDMO.
More than 15 new oncology generic products to be completed in FY27.
Enzalutamide, Abraxane and Rotigotine patch launches on track for FY28; Rotigotine now expected in H1 FY28 after a two-quarter delay from a European raw-material variation approval.
Ondansetron India launch expected in H1 FY28, pending state approvals and licences after central approval.
Nivolumab biosimilar to be filed in Europe next year (FY28); Aflibercept to be in the Indian market in FY27.
Recombinant albumin Phase III protocol approved by CDSCO and EMA; IMPD submission in Europe targeted for H2 FY27.
Peptide volume and utilisation commentary deferred to H2 of next year; albumin and excipient revenue visibility deferred to around FY28.
capex_capacity: INR252 crores capex spent in H1 FY27, funded by internal accruals.

Peptides: 4 manufacturing lines in operation, 2 more being added, with space kept for further expansion. One of the largest integrated peptide capacities in India to be commissioned by end FY27; the USD 50 million peptide investment is phased and depends on utilisation.
Peptide capacity is aimed at a mix of CDMO, GLP-1 and HPAPI; management did not disclose kilolitres or gross block.
Biologics plant at Dharwad is ready and approved, and the fermentation unit is audit-ready.
Jadcherla (US FDA) is under remediation; EU authorities re-inspected and cleared the plant. US critical filings have been moved to CMO sites.
demand_pricing: Gross margin fell about 700 bps YoY and QoQ. Management attributed this to the mix shift toward lower-margin API sales and higher global API raw material costs, and said it would persist until raw material prices settle.

Nilotinib faces new generic entrants in Europe, but management sees no big change in numbers because the product is tender-based with 1–3 year tenders. Axitinib already had multiple generic players at launch.
Nor-UDCA (NAFLD) has had zero recalls in its first year since launch.
Three complex 505(b)(2) products are commercialised, with 5-plus more in advanced development for launch over the next 2–3 years.
Biosimilar pipeline: 7 active molecules with average global sales above USD10 billion; 2 biosimilars entering human studies for EU/RoW in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall about 700 bps, and how much cost increase has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Bhutada said the strong API quarter (lower-margin) versus higher-margin formulation drove the decline. Basant Bansal's follow-up got a confirmation that raw material cost to sales rose from 28.65% to 35.72% due to higher API sales and global API raw material inflation, which will persist until prices settle.

qa_highlights.question: What peptide capacity is planned, and what utilisation is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is built for tonnage-scale annual volumes, and utilisation depends on customer uptake. It will comment in H2 of next year, and there is visibility on some programs that require volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Which biosimilar is closest to approval, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Nivolumab is the closest. It is planned for filing in Europe next year. Aflibercept will be in India in FY27, and Adalimumab is already marketed in India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CDMO outlook for FY28 and the late-stage programs?
qa_highlights.answer: Four late-stage programs are under registration and two are in Phase III. At least one is expected to commercialise next year and three the year after. In three of them, Shilpa supplies the API.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the CDMO platform carved out from API?
qa_highlights.answer: As a one-stop integrated partner (KSM to final API for peptides; clone development to fill-finish for biologics; in-house payload, linker, antibody and conjugation for ADC), it aims to win more programs each year. Management confirmed the carve-out was to serve CDMO clients better.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Jadcherla with the US FDA and the plant risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working with the US FDA on remediation, with no impact on revenues or the 2–3 year plan. The EU re-inspected and cleared the plant, and most US critical filings are moved to CMO sites.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Rotigotine delayed, and when will it launch?
qa_highlights.answer: A European variation approval for one raw material took an extra two quarters. The launch is now set for H1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of biologics revenue is licensing versus CDMO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said each quarter will carry a mix of CDMO, biosimilar and licensing revenue, and did not break it out.

qa_highlights.question: What share of service and licensing income is licensing, and is its gross margin 100%?
qa_highlights.answer: Alpesh Dalal declined to give the licensing split or assume 100% margin. He said there are no COGS, but related R&D and other expenses sit in those lines.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from API raw material inflation and API mix; watch whether it eases once raw material prices settle.
Regulatory: Jadcherla US FDA remediation remains open; US supply now depends on CMO sites.
Timing risk on launches: Rotigotine has slipped by two quarters, and Ondansetron depends on state approvals.
Peptide capacity is ahead of confirmed orders; utilisation disclosure deferred to H2 FY28.
Nilotinib generic competition in Europe, and the tender-based pricing that governs it.
Biologics earnings quality: lumpy licensing income versus recurring CDMO and biosimilar revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the strategic story, with record numbers highlighted. Management was guarded and deflective on forward numbers, repeatedly declining revenue, utilisation, oncology split and licensing-share questions, and pointing to the investor presentation instead.
key_quotes: The years of harvesting are beginning.
For the second quarter, we posted our highest ever revenue and highest ever EBITDA, backed by growth in all 4 business segments.
So there are no risks that we see to our revenues from the Jadcherla plant.
But we do not provide any revenue guidance or revenue indication.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New product launch

tone.note: Management was confident on the record H1 and the oncology and CDMO pipeline, but guarded on peptide utilisation, licensing split and forward numbers. Analysts pushed on the 700 bps gross margin fall and how much raw material inflation had been passed on.
